findings.note: A granted override that lapses can be recorded as FIXED in the same Reconcile pass, which breaks the invariant this package states explicitly. internal/findings/bind.go:111 turns an overridden record into status "open", and internal/findings/findings.go:115 runs that before the open->fixed transition at findings.go:144-153, whose guard accepts status "open". internal/findings/findings.go:142-143 says the opposite is intended: "StatusOverridden is deliberately not included: a granted override is an acknowledged exception, never a fix, and its fixedInRunId stays empty so post-merge learning can tell the two apart" - and CLAUDE.md repeats it ("an override is never a fix (fixedInRunId stays empty)"). Before this diff `overridden` was terminal so the fix branch was unreachable from it; the new lapse transition opens that route. Concrete failure, verified by a probe test in package findings (temporarily added, run, then deleted): seed an open blocker with fingerprint pr:some-lint:internal/x.go and RunID mrv-run-1, RequestOverride then GrantOverride (status overridden, kind paths), edit internal/x.go, then Reconcile with run mrv-run-2 and Options{PreviousRunID: "mrv-run-1"} and NO current inputs carrying that fingerprint. Observed result: status="fixed", fixedInRunId="mrv-run-2", overrideGrantedBy="dsifry@warmstart.ai", overrideLapsedAt set. The "no current inputs" precondition is not exotic and this PR makes it more likely, not less: mutation findings only exist when --mutation-report is passed (cmd/metareview/main.go:224,263,295), so run 1 with the flag files a survivor blocker, an override is granted, and the ordinary repair re-run `--previous-run <run-1>` without the flag lapses the override and immediately closes it as fixed. Damage: (a) fixedInRunId now asserts a fix that never happened, so post-merge learning counts an exception as a resolution - the exact confusion findings.go:142 exists to prevent; (b) internal/findings/override.go:170-186 overrideLines renders only override-pending and overridden, so the exception disappears from the "Process Overrides" section of docs/metareview/FINDINGS.md and from `override list` entirely, leaving no visible trail that a grant lapsed; (c) the operator gets no signal from UnresolvedBlocking that an exception has lapsed. The gate itself is not left open (a fixed record no longer suppresses rediscovery, so a later run that re-reports the fingerprint files a fresh blocker), which is why this is medium and not high. Suggested repair: exclude records carrying a non-empty OverrideGrantedAt (or OverrideLapsedAt set in this pass) from the open->fixed transition, or lapse to StatusOverridePending instead of "open" so the record keeps blocking and stays in the override ledger until someone re-grants or fixes it.

A mistyped `--target` value makes `status --json` report blocked:false, so a host hook wired to that field fails open. cmd/metareview/main.go:117 passes the operator's raw string straight to status.EmitFor with no normalisation or existence check, and internal/status/status.go:186-196 matches it by exact string equality against reviewlog target ids (`s.Target != target -> continue`), so a target nobody has ever reviewed yields must_clear=[] and exit 0 - indistinguishable from a genuinely clean target. Failure scenario: a hook computes the target as "./docs/plan.md" or "t_1" where the log recorded "docs/plan.md" or "t-1", the gate that is supposed to enforce the Completion Rule silently permits the work, and nothing in the exit code or `blocked` says the scope matched nothing. Uncertainty stated: this is the documented and intended design (the comment at main.go:113-115 argues the unscoped alternative is a livelock, and tests/go/test-cli-baseline.sh:59 asserts exit 0 for an unreviewed target), and a caller can distinguish the two cases today by noticing that the scoped `reviews` array is empty - so this is a hardening request, not a defect: consider echoing a match count or a `target_known` boolean so a shell hook does not have to parse the reviews array to tell a typo from a clean corner. Kept low because the matching itself lives in internal/status/status.go, which is shard-4's subject, not this shard's.
